name: Christ the Redeemer, Rio de Janeiro
fact: One of the most photogrammetry-scanned landmarks on Earth, showing up in nearly every 3D Tiles demo reel.

name: Half Dome, Yosemite
fact: Its granite face has been laser-scanned so many times it practically has its own point cloud fandom.

name: Mount Everest, Himalayas
fact: Its official height has been re-surveyed multiple times, most recently jointly by Nepal and China in 2020.

name: Sydney Opera House, Australia
fact: Its curved shells were originally impossible to engineer until someone realized they could all be cut from the same sphere.

name: Grand Canyon, Arizona
fact: A favorite terrain-tile stress test since it has both massive scale and brutal elevation changes.

name: Burj Khalifa, Dubai
fact: Tall enough that its upper floors see the sunset several minutes later than street level.

name: CN Tower, Toronto
fact: Held the record for the world's tallest freestanding structure for over 30 years.

name: McMurdo Station, Antarctica
fact: One of the few places on Earth where satellite imagery updates are more exciting than the local news.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza, Egypt
fact: Its base is level to within about 2 centimeters, still baffling modern engineers.

name: Apple Park, Cupertino
fact: Nicknamed 'The Spaceship,' this massive ring-shaped building is a marvel of curved glass.

name: Mount Fuji, Japan
fact: Its near-perfect symmetry makes it one of the most recognizable digital elevation models in any dataset.

name: Þingvellir Rift, Iceland
fact: You can literally stand between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates as they slowly pull apart.

name: MIT Stata Center, Cambridge
fact: Its deconstructivist architecture is so wildly complex it practically demands to be viewed in a 3D environment.

name: Moscone Center, San Francisco
fact: The epicenter of game developer conferences and the birthplace of countless immersive tech hackathons.

name: Downtown Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
fact: Home to William Penn atop City Hall, looking over a dense, thriving spatial computing and tech community.

name: Times Square, New York City
fact: A glowing hub of digital displays, massive crowds, and a frequent backdrop for immersive tech awards ceremonies.

name: Wembley Stadium, London
fact: An iconic venue for international soccer tournaments, featuring a massive 133-meter-tall arch.

name: Alpe d'Huez, France
fact: One of the most legendary climbs in cycling, its 21 switchbacks look incredible rendered in 3D terrain.

name: Meta Headquarters, Menlo Park
fact: Ground zero for major developments in extended reality, spatial computing platforms, and open-source models.

name: Eiffel Tower, Paris
fact: Originally intended to be a temporary installation, it is now one of the most recognizable structures on the globe.

name: Machu Picchu, Peru
fact: An Incan citadel set high in the Andes Mountains, providing some of the most dramatic 3D terrain elevation data available.

name: Colosseum, Rome
fact: The largest ancient amphitheater ever built, offering a fascinating structural scan for geospatial visualization.

name: Estadio Azteca, Mexico City
fact: A historic soccer cathedral that has hosted two FIFA World Cup finals and sits at a demanding high altitude.

name: Petra, Jordan
fact: Famous for its rock-cut architecture, this archaeological site is nestled deep within narrow desert canyons.

name: Taj Mahal, India
fact: An immense mausoleum of white marble, renowned for its perfect symmetry and intricate optical illusions.

name: Angkor Wat, Cambodia
fact: The largest religious monument in the world, spanning a massive temple complex integrated closely with the jungle.

name: Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco
fact: A suspension bridge connecting San Francisco Bay to the Pacific, famously painted 'International Orange'.

name: Niagara Falls, Canada/USA
fact: A group of three massive waterfalls that straddle the international border, moving an astonishing volume of water.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro, Tanzania
fact: The highest single free-standing mountain above sea level in the world, featuring three distinct volcanic cones.

name: Venice Canals, Italy
fact: A city built on more than 100 small islands in a lagoon, making its geospatial mapping heavily reliant on water levels.

name: Sagrada Familia, Barcelona
fact: Antoni Gaudí's masterpiece has been under construction since 1882 and features wildly complex organic geometry.

name: Milford Sound, New Zealand
fact: A stunning fiord carved by glaciers, surrounded by sheer rock faces that rise thousands of feet straight out of the water.

name: Vatnajökull Glacier, Iceland
fact: The largest ice cap in Iceland, covering active volcanoes and providing an intense white-out contrast in 3D data.

name: Empire State Building, New York
fact: Constructed in just 410 days during the Great Depression, an unbelievable feat of engineering logistics.

name: Camp Nou, Barcelona
fact: The largest stadium in Spain and Europe, a legendary stomping ground for some of soccer's greatest players.

name: Col de du Tourmalet, France
fact: The highest paved mountain pass in the French Pyrenees, infamous for its punishing gradients in grand tour cycling.

name: Marina Bay Sands, Singapore
fact: Features a massive 340-meter-long SkyPark balancing across three separate 55-story hotel towers.

name: Petronas Twin Towers, Malaysia
fact: Connected by a double-decker skybridge that is designed to slide in and out of the towers to prevent wind damage.

name: Table Mountain, South Africa
fact: A flat-topped mountain forming a prominent landmark overlooking the city of Cape Town.

name: Mount St. Helens, Washington
fact: The 1980 eruption blew 1,300 feet off the top of the mountain, leaving a massive, highly-scanned horseshoe crater.

name: Burj Al Arab, Dubai
fact: Designed to mimic the sail of a ship, it stands on an artificial island completely separate from the mainland.

name: Stonehenge, United Kingdom
fact: A prehistoric stone circle aligned with the solstices, sitting prominently in the middle of a vast chalk moorland.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle, Germany
fact: The ultimate fairytale castle perched on a rugged hill in Bavaria, and the inspiration for Disneyland's Sleeping Beauty Castle.

name: The Matterhorn, Swiss/Italian Border
fact: A near-perfect pyramidal peak that serves as one of the most iconic and dangerous mountains in the Alps.

name: Guggenheim Museum, Bilbao
fact: Designed by Frank Gehry using early 3D aerospace software (CATIA) to calculate its impossible titanium curves.

name: Salar de Uyuni, Bolivia
fact: The world's largest salt flat. It is so flat and reflective that satellites use it to calibrate their altimeters.

name: Acropolis of Athens, Greece
fact: An ancient citadel located on a rocky outcrop above the city, containing the remains of the Parthenon.

name: Santiago Bernabéu Stadium, Madrid
fact: One of the world's most famous and prestigious football venues, recently wrapped in a massive, futuristic steel facade.

name: The Palm Jumeirah, Dubai
fact: An archipelago of artificial islands created using land reclamation, shaped like a massive palm tree.

name: Chichén Itzá, Mexico
fact: A massive pre-Columbian city built by the Maya people, dominated by the Temple of Kukulcán.

name: Grand Prismatic Spring, Yellowstone
fact: The largest hot spring in the US, known for its striking bands of bright colors created by microbial mats.

name: San Siro Stadium, Milan
fact: Distinctive for its massive cylindrical concrete towers that support the roof and serve as pedestrian ramps.

name: Arecibo Observatory, Puerto Rico
fact: Though the massive radio telescope collapsed in 2020, its enormous sinkhole footprint remains a topographical anomaly.

name: Potala Palace, Tibet
fact: Sitting at an elevation of 12,100 feet, this massive fortress-like structure dominates the Lhasa valley.

name: Uluru (Ayers Rock), Australia
fact: A massive sandstone monolith in the heart of the Northern Territory's arid 'Red Centre'.

name: Passo dello Stelvio, Italy
fact: The highest paved mountain pass in the Eastern Alps, featuring an iconic ribbon of 48 hairpin turns.

name: Hoover Dam, Nevada/Arizona
fact: A colossal concrete arch-gravity dam in the Black Canyon of the Colorado River.

name: Giant's Causeway, Northern Ireland
fact: An area of about 40,000 interlocking basalt columns, the result of an ancient volcanic fissure eruption.

name: Seattle Space Needle, Washington
fact: Built for the 1962 World's Fair, it was designed to withstand winds of 200 mph and earthquakes up to a 9.0 magnitude.

name: Cliffs of Moher, Ireland
fact: Sea cliffs running for 14 kilometers along the Atlantic Ocean, dropping sharply down to the crashing waves below.

name: Ha Long Bay, Vietnam
fact: Features thousands of towering limestone karsts and isles jutting dramatically out of emerald waters.

name: Allianz Arena, Munich
fact: Known as the 'inflatable boat' due to its exterior of inflated ETFE plastic panels that can change color.

name: Maracanã Stadium, Rio de Janeiro
fact: An iconic soccer venue that held nearly 200,000 spectators during the 1950 World Cup final.

name: Crater Lake, Oregon
fact: Formed by the collapse of a volcano, it is the deepest lake in the United States.

name: Delicate Arch, Utah
fact: A 52-foot-tall freestanding natural arch carved by wind and sand out of Entrada Sandstone.

name: Victoria Falls, Zambia/Zimbabwe
fact: Considered the largest waterfall in the world by the combined width and height of its falling water sheet.

name: The Gherkin (30 St Mary Axe), London
fact: Its aerodynamic shape is designed to minimize wind turbulence down at street level.

name: Gateway Arch, St. Louis
fact: The world's tallest arch, built as a mathematically perfect inverted catenary curve.

name: Mount Etna, Italy
fact: One of the most active volcanoes in the world, constantly altering its own 3D topography.

name: Louvre Museum, Paris
fact: The world's most-visited museum, famous for the stark contrast between its historic palace and modern glass pyramid.

name: Panama Canal (Miraflores Locks)
fact: An artificial 82 km waterway that connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, utilizing a massive lock system.

name: Iguazú Falls, Argentina/Brazil
fact: A massive waterfall system comprised of 275 individual drops spread across a 2.7-kilometer edge.

name: Angel Falls, Venezuela
fact: The world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, dropping 3,212 feet from the edge of the Auyán-tepui mountain.

name: Banff National Park (Lake Louise), Canada
fact: A glacial lake known for its shocking turquoise color, surrounded by towering, jagged peaks.

name: White Cliffs of Dover, United Kingdom
fact: Iconic chalk cliffs facing the Strait of Dover, composed primarily of microscopic skeletal remains.

name: Pamukkale, Turkey
fact: Famous for its dazzling white terraces of travertine, created by carbonate minerals left by flowing water.

name: Zhangjiajie National Forest, China
fact: Home to towering pillar-like karst formations that famously inspired the floating mountains in the movie Avatar.

name: Great Blue Hole, Belize
fact: A giant marine sinkhole near the center of Lighthouse Reef, originally formed as a limestone cave during the last ice age.

name: Koppenberg, Belgium
fact: A notorious, brutally steep cobblestone climb that often forces professional cyclists off their bikes.

name: Walt Disney Concert Hall, Los Angeles
fact: Frank Gehry's sweeping metallic surfaces originally reflected so much sunlight they melted nearby traffic cones.

name: Kennedy Space Center (Launch Complex 39A)
fact: The historic launch pad where the Apollo 11 mission departed for the moon, now utilized for modern spaceflight.

name: The Great Sphinx of Giza, Egypt
fact: Carved directly out of a single piece of limestone bedrock, making it the oldest known monumental sculpture in Egypt.

name: Easter Island (Ahu Tongariki), Chile
fact: The largest ahu (shrine) on Easter Island, featuring 15 massive restored Moai statues facing inland.

name: CERN (The Globe of Science), Switzerland
fact: The surface-level visitor center sitting directly above the massive subterranean Large Hadron Collider ring.

name: Taipei 101, Taiwan
fact: Built to withstand Pacific Rim earthquakes, it contains a massive 660-ton tuned mass damper suspended near the top.

name: Oriental Pearl Tower, Shanghai
fact: A distinct TV tower characterized by its 11 varying-sized spheres linked by colossal columns.

name: Old Trafford Stadium, Manchester
fact: Known as the 'Theatre of Dreams,' it is the largest club football stadium in the United Kingdom.

name: Mont Blanc, France/Italy
fact: The highest mountain in the Alps, featuring dramatic, deeply crevassed glaciers dominating its flanks.

name: Chrysler Building, New York
fact: An Art Deco masterpiece famous for its terraced crown, secretly constructed inside the building and raised in one piece.

name: Seattle Spheres, Washington
fact: Three intersecting glass domes serving as an indoor rainforest workspace for Amazon employees in downtown Seattle.

name: Flatiron Building, New York
fact: A triangular steel-framed landmark that was never actually the tallest building in New York, despite popular belief.

name: La Bombonera, Buenos Aires
fact: A stadium with a highly unusual 'D' shape, known for acoustics so intense the concrete literally vibrates.

name: Pico de Veleta, Spain
fact: The highest paved road in Europe, offering an exhausting, high-altitude challenge for serious cyclists.

name: Gyeongbokgung Palace, Seoul
fact: The largest of the Five Grand Palaces built by the Joseon dynasty, sitting beautifully against a mountainous backdrop.

name: Mount Aconcagua, Argentina
fact: The highest mountain in the Americas and the highest outside of Asia, boasting massive, sweeping scree slopes.

name: Vessel, Hudson Yards NYC
fact: A massive, honeycomb-like structural artwork consisting of 154 intricately interconnecting flights of stairs.

name: The Eden Project, UK
fact: Massive hexagonal and pentagonal ETFE biomes nestled inside a reclaimed china clay pit in Cornwall.

name: Meteor Crater, Arizona
fact: The world's best-preserved meteorite impact site, forming a perfect 4,000-foot-wide bowl in the desert.

name: Lotus Temple, New Delhi
fact: A Bahá'í House of Worship composed of 27 free-standing marble-clad 'petals' arranged in clusters.

name: Kjeragbolten, Norway
fact: A massive 5-cubic-meter glacial boulder suspended in a mountain crevice 3,228 feet directly above an abyss.
